text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak said there would be stability in the region unless agreements signed by the Palestinians and the Israelis are implemented. He said it would dangerous to go back to square one in peace negotiations or renegotiate agreements.

- As part of celebrations of the October 1973 victory, the armed forces in Ismailia are organising military parades and sports and music shows starting with a paratrooper drop and shows expressing joy at the reopening of the Suez Canal.
- Nile waters flowed into the Toshka overflow yesterday for the first time.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat today briefs Mubarak on the results of his talks with U.S. Secretray of State Warren Christopher and the state of talks with Israel.
- Sheikh Shaarawi denies that he endorsed an attempt by Ahmed Sabahi, leader of the Egyptian Umma Party, to set himself up as spiritual leader and imam of all Moslems.

- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi said the Badr 96 manoeuvres held last month were part of an annual and five-year plan and the aim was to measure the effectiveness of the units of the armed forces.
- Mubarak says no development without peace. The idea of renegotiations puts the region at risk of disaster.

- An inventory of museums has found a number of serious irregularities. Some museum pieces are not registered, the registers are old and contain many mistakes and omissions. Officials from four museums will be investigated for neglect.

- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, in an interview with Mayo, says military force is a tool to impose peace and that President Mubarak's decision not to attend the Washington summit shows the depth of his vision and perspicacity. The Sudanese regime cannot threaten Egypt. Rest assured... We are in full control of our borders.
- The number of candidates in trade union elections has risen to 25,000.
- Mubarak had phone calls on Sunday from Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi and Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
- There are various interpretations of the Constitutional Court's ruling that it is unconstitutional for the public prosecutor to freeze the assets of defendants.
